b: Total Chess – Group Stage, Day 4 (14 November 2026)
On each day of the group stage, the players face each other twice, with colours reversed in the second game. The first game starts at 15:00, the second at 18:30.

The Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot takes place from 10 to 20 November at the Anantara New York Palace Hotel in Budapest. Developed by Norway Chess and approved by FIDE, the competition combines three different time controls. The event serves as a test for the Total Chess World Championship Tour, which is scheduled to begin in 2027.
The 24 participants include Magnus Carlsen, Fabiano Caruana, Vincent Keymer, Wesley So, Anish Giri, Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Hungary's Richard Rapport.
The tournament consists of three stages:

Blitz tournament (10 November): The event begins with all 24 participants playing nine rounds of blitz chess (3+2) under the Swiss system. The final standings will later serve as a tiebreak and influence the pairings in the knockout stage. Magnus Carlsen won ahead of Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Levon Aronian.

Group stage (11–15 November): The players are divided into four groups of six. Within each group, everyone plays everyone else twice, once with White and once with Black. The time control is 45 minutes plus 30 seconds per move. A win earns three points and a draw one point. The games are rated and count towards the FIDE rating list.

Knockout stage (17–20 November): After a rest day, the players are divided into six separate knockout competitions according to their group-stage standings. Only the four group winners compete for the overall tournament victory. Each knockout match lasts two days. On each day, the players contest four blitz games, two rapid games (15+10) and one game with 45 minutes plus 30 seconds per move. Games played at longer time controls carry more weight than blitz games. If the match remains tied after the two days, an Armageddon game decides the winner.
